title: Social and professional contexts of legal commitment
shortTitle: Social and professional contexts of legal commitment
summary: Intention concerning legal enforceability asks whether the parties’ undertaking belongs to a relationship the law will treat as contractually binding in the circumstances.
notes:
The readings distinguish a serious moral or social commitment from an enforceable contractual undertaking. Balfour’s judges give related but distinct reasons concerning a domestic allowance. Cohen rejects the contract claim in its journalistic setting but later allows recovery through promissory estoppel. A statement that a promise is morally important does not settle either legal question. Identify the context and the ground actually used by the particular court.

Cohen’s earlier opinion treats the source-reporter promise as ethically serious but unsuitable for an ordinary contract theory; the later opinion allows estoppel. Social arrangements, rides, family commitments, and medical reassurance raise related contextual issues. The Balfour opinion is in the course supplement (pp. 11–20) and briefed in its own entry; the casebook’s references place it here. The text also distinguishes unmarried parties’ capacity to contract from assumptions drawn from marriage or family relations.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 183–187. Open assigned page 183.
